newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' AsianBank 1996 net up 97 percent.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' AsianBank 1996 net up 97 percent.

text.p: Unlisted AsianBank Corporation said on Wednesday it posted a 97 percent growth in net income in 1996 to 400.4 million pesos from 203.6 million pesos in 1995.
AsianBank and PDCP Development Bank have agreed to merge later this year. AsianBank is currently 41 percent-owned by holding firm A. Soriano Corp.
The bank said its net interest income jumped by 49 percent in 1996 to 700.5 million pesos.
"Strong growth rates for loans and deposits were posted as a vibrant business climate heightened the need for banking services," it said.
When the merger is completed with PDCP, the newly formed AsianBank Corp will have 140 branches and 6.6 billion pesos in capital, the bank said.
The AB Capital Group, which is affiliated with AsianBank Corp, reported a net income of 140.6 million pesos in 1996.
The AB Capital Group focuses on the capital market and includes AB Capital and Investment Corp, Anscor Hagedorn Securities Inc and AB Leasing and Finance Corp.
AB Capital and Investment Corp is 32.4 percent-owned by A. Soriano Corp, while the securities and leasing firms are directly owned by AB Capital and Investment Corp.
